clue.text: Special pal you primarily had on team, perhaps

definitions.text: Special pal you primarily had on team, perhaps

indicators.note: special in the sense of specially made up, telling us to rework the letters that follow
primarily means only the first letter of the word you is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone reminisces about a particular friend who was on their side in a team game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' reworks PAL, Y (the first letter of 'you', picked out by 'primarily') and TEAM; 'had on' just joins them. The whole clue also describes a childhood friend you played alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A childhood companion in games is exactly a friend you were teamed with, so the whole clue serves as the definition.

clue.text: Suffer thus in test for container of 8

indicators.note: the answer placed thus inside the word test makes the container, so taking test away from the container leaves it

parts.note: 8 across is the drink black tea, and a tea chest is the box it is shipped in
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is put through a painful test involving a tea box.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: 'thus in' means the answer, placed inside the word test, would make the container of 8 across, a tea chest. Removing that word's letters from the container recovers the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to feel pain, a plain synonym for suffering.

clue.text: Carrier of note, in a way unpleasant

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a common abbreviation for a way
icky is informal for nasty or unpleasant

explanation.surface: A musical courier travels along a road with something disagreeable about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrier of note' sounds like a musician or messenger, but it is a self-adhesive notelet that carries a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky is an informal name for a self-adhesive slip of paper, which carries a written message.

clue.text: Finish up splitting fish of rotten quality

indicators.note: splitting means breaking the fish apart and sitting in its middle

parts.note: the bass is a fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a finish is an end

explanation.surface: A completed task divides a catch of fish that is going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the finish word backwards in this down entry, and 'splitting' drives it into the middle of the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Badness is the state of being bad, which is what rotten quality amounts to.

clue.text: Waive a rule, ie bad act that needs changing

indicators.note: the phrase says these letters must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone excuses a regulation because some bad behaviour has to be corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that needs changing' rearranges IEBADACT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne, renouncing one's rule or reign.

clue.text: Stoppages slow down vehicles, we hear, on hills

indicators.note: we hear tells us to take the spoken sound, not the written word

parts.note: to brake is to slow down vehicles
downs are rolling chalk hills, as in the South Downs of England

explanation.surface: Traffic delays happen when cars must slow down over hilly country.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAKE and BREAK sound alike, as 'we hear' signals; 'on' places it above DOWNS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakdowns are failures that bring machines or processes to a halt, i.e. stoppages.

clue.text: Somewhat romantically, predicting the future

indicators.note: somewhat means only some of the word romantically is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller makes rather dreamy forecasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in roMANTICally.
explanation.definitionFit: Mantic is a rare adjective meaning relating to divination or prophecy.

clue.text: Drink with meal on jet

indicators.note: in an across clue, meal on jet means the meal word comes after the jet word

parts.note: jet black, so jet means black
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A drink is served with food aboard an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' looks like an aircraft, but it is the glossy black stone, hence the colour; in an across clue 'on' puts the meal second.
explanation.definitionFit: Black tea is tea taken without milk, a drink.

clue.text: Apart from Spanish white wine, mostly French white wine

parts.note: bar means except, apart from

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: sack is an old name for a white wine from Spain, as drunk by Falstaff

explanation.surface: A wine list skips the Spanish white in favour of mostly French ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the old Spanish wine name. 'white wine' appears twice to mislead: only the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Part-time medic's alter ego

parts.note: Dr Jekyll is only a doctor some of the time; his other self is the brutal figure in Stevenson's story

explanation.surface: A locum doctor leads a double life.
explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's tale Dr Jekyll is a doctor only part of the time, turning into his evil other self the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In R L Stevenson's novella the respectable doctor Jekyll's evil second personality is Mr Hyde.

clue.text: Study poem returned by poet's girlfriend

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling
Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A poet's lover examines a verse sent back to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses the title of Kipling's poem. 'girlfriend' is fair because the answer means a female confidant.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidante is a woman in whom one confides, a close female friend.

clue.text: Tribesman, cunning and irritating person

parts.note: Gad was a son of Jacob and founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel
fly is British slang for sharp or cunning

explanation.surface: A list describes a clansman as both crafty and annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is a horsefly, and figuratively someone who persistently provokes or annoys others.

clue.text: Ornamentation on bow or top of violin

definitions.meaning: a carved scroll decoration at the prow of a ship
the scroll head at the top of a violin's neck

explanation.surface: Musical decoration is placed on the violin's bow or its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests a violin bow but is the front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a scroll carving on a ship's prow and the scroll of a violin, which is also a fiddle.

clue.text: Fruit and fish on quay (or second fish)

parts.note: the shad is a fish of the herring family
a dock is a quay or wharf

explanation.surface: A harbour market sells fruit and fish on the waterside.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket offers an alternative parse: S (second) plus HADDOCK (fish) gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock is the pomelo, a large citrus fruit.

clue.text: Observing in no-man's-land, thus revealing what can be found here (above and below)

definitions.text: revealing what can be found here (above and below)

parts.note: observing, as in perusing text, means reading it
no-man's-land lay ... the opposing trench lines in the First World War

explanation.surface: A soldier watches the ground between the trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is idiomatic: finding hidden meaning, as the clues above and below hide words (MANTIC in 'romantically', HERMES in 'other messengers').
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means detecting a meaning that is not openly stated, as hidden words in nearby clues are.

clue.text: It's not simple aboard, inside cabins at sea

indicators.note: inside puts one piece within the other
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
on means aboard, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A ship's accommodation is described as complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' jumbles the cabins to give NBASIC, and 'inside' places the word for aboard within it. The ship imagery makes 'aboard' look like setting rather than wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonbasic means not elementary, i.e. not simple.

clue.text: See 15
Part of telescope I reportedly mounted on castle, for example

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we take the spoken sound

parts.note: the letter I is pronounced like the word for the organ of sight
a castle, or rook, is one example of a chess piece

explanation.surface: An astronomer climbs a castle with part of a telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted on' puts the sound-alike above PIECE in this down entry; 'castle' is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyepiece is the lens at the end of a telescope that the viewer looks through.

clue.text: Provides help as stupid creature is crossing street

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, proverbially stupid

indicators.note: crossing means is goes across, around, the street

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone helps as a donkey wanders across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' means the short form for street lies inside 'is', not that an animal crosses a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Assists means aids or helps, a straightforward synonym for provides help.

clue.text: See 15
Messenger hidden by other messengers

indicators.note: hidden by says the answer is concealed among the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A courier is concealed among a group of other couriers.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in otHER MESsengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermes is the messenger of the gods in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Thin slice of meat less well considered

definitions.meaning: a thin strip of bacon or ham
more impetuous, comparing someone hasty with another

explanation.surface: A butcher's thin cut was a hastier choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a slice of bacon, and as a comparative of rash it means more hasty and less thoughtful.

clue.text: Run round a lot as a nomad

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is round in shape
many means a lot

explanation.surface: A wanderer runs around a great deal, like a traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romany is a member of the traditionally travelling Roma people, a nomad.

clue.text: One who composed mass about an island's religious practice

indicators.note: about means the composer and mass go around the other pieces

parts.note: Johannes Brahms was a composer
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A composer's setting of a Mass reflects an island's religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the composer plus the mass symbol around 'an' and the island letter. 'mass' looks like a church service, which suits the religious surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahmanism is the ancient religion of India, the forerunner of Hinduism, a religious system and practice.

clue.text: Alliance of states taking boundary area back

indicators.note: back means the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: in cricket a boundary is a hit over the rope scoring six

explanation.surface: A coalition of nations reclaims a border region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundary' looks like a frontier but is the cricket hit worth SIX runs; 'back' turns SIX + A round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan; the word generally means a pact between states.

clue.text: Artist endlessly climbing over the hill

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters read upwards, so backwards
endlessly means the final letter is removed

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French painter

explanation.surface: A painter keeps scaling a hill without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims DEGAS to DEGA, and 'climbing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the hill is an idiom for old and past one's best, so it means aged.

clue.text: Alpine characters shifted from mountainous region

indicators.note: shifted means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Letters in a word about the Alps get moved away from the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' rearranges ALPINE; 'characters' just says the letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepali means belonging to Nepal, the Himalayan country, a mountainous region.

clue.text: Number of political leaders won't admit embracing Conservative inclination

parts.note: Number 10 Downing Street is the British prime minister's residence

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: to deny is to refuse to admit

explanation.surface: Party chiefs refuse to accept a Tory leaning.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN is the number of the house of Britain's prime minister, 10 Downing Street. 'embracing' puts C in DENY: DEN-C-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is a leaning or disposition, the same as an inclination.
